verdict.rationale: Semgrep Secrets' own docs say it validates detected secrets against the issuing web service and marks as 'valid' those confirmed to grant access. It uses that validity status to prioritize findings and to notify developers in PRs and MRs, which is the core of the story. Missing for 10: documentation of which services or providers have validators, how invalid or unverifiable results are reported, and independent or hands-on corroboration that validation works.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can have detected secrets verified against the issuing service so I know which ones are live

citations.quote: valid secrets are those that have been tested against a web service and confirmed to successfully grant resources or authentication. They are actively in use.
